Design research

Pass 9's image loop, start to finish: the Gemini concepts for each section, every image taken apart into words, the themes and design choices they add up to, the build notes, and the skills that run it again.

OverviewConceptsImages taken apartThemes and keywordsStyle atlasBuild notesSkills and briefs

What this is

Pass 9 asked for every section of the site to become its own bold design instead of "tabular data all the way down". Each section got a concept image from Gemini, and every image was then read back into words, so the look we were reaching for could be named, counted and reused. This page holds all of it: every concept, what each section became, every image taken apart into keywords, the themes they add up to, the build notes, and the skills that run the loop again.

The images are ideas, not the brand: their fonts, logos, copy and figures are invented by the image model. Each was rebuilt with Aquemi tokens, type and real content.

The loop: image → text → image

  1. 1

    Page copy

    Each section of the 27 pages, with its real text

    content/pages/*.json
  2. 2

    Section prompt

    Base + the section's content + one art direction + negatives from the atlas

    tools/section_prompts.py, kit.json
  3. 3

    Gemini concept

    Edit the chat's first prompt and resend, so each image starts fresh; capture full size

    gemini-helpers.js, save_capture.py
  4. 4

    Describe

    Each image back to text: style family, palette, type, layout devices, 25 to 40 keywords, a reusable prompt

    describe.workflow.js → style-atlas/images/*.json
  5. 5

    Atlas

    Count it all: brand core, ten families, what combines, what fails, the prompt kit

    aggregate.py → keywords.json, STYLE-ATLAS.md
  6. 6

    Build and ship

    One look per section from its concept, motion from the library; checked at 1280 and 375

    look-*.js, ship.sh, versions.py

Stages 2 to 5 run again as one loop: new images are described, the atlas is refreshed, and the next prompts come from its kit. The image-prompt-loop skill runs it.

Where we stopped

The Gemini image quota ran out twice. Sections without a concept were built from ideas in the pool (their build notes say which).

  • Pass 9 QUOTA at compliance.4 (Gemini: 'I can create more images as soon as your limit resets'); compliance.4 not generated. Not done: compliance.4 to sys-storage.4, then redo systems.0, systems.1 (old prompt) and home.0-4 with new mids
  • Pass 9b STOPPED at svc-fabrication.3 (sent, not captured): after the reload the pass-9 chat and the whole chat history stopped rendering (empty conversation, empty sidebar) through 5 reloads over ~6 min; no quota message seen. Resume from svc-fabrication.3 (queue index 24).
  • Pass 9b RESUME ATTEMPT: pass-9 chat still blank after reload. Started ONE new chat (Pro): https://gemini.google.com/app/cf066e2f02a40e33 with svc-fabrication.3 as its first prompt; it generated an image (seen in the live page), but reloading that chat also renders blank (no messages, empty sidebar) after 20 s+, so it could not be captured. STOPPED again at svc-fabrication.3 (index 24); 57 items left.
  • Pass 9b RESUMED in new chat https://gemini.google.com/app/cf066e2f02a40e33 (loaded on the 3rd 60 s retry).
  • Pass 9b STOPPED at svc-fat-sat.0 (index 25; sent to the new chat, not captured): reload blank again after generation; 3 retries at 60 s failed. 55 items left (svc-fat-sat.0 onward).
  • Pass 9b QUOTA at svc-fat-sat.3 (reset: Nov 1, 5:57 PM per the model menu; Flash, 3.1 Pro and Argon all limited). Resume at queue index 29 (svc-fat-sat.3).
  • Pass 9b QUOTA at ind-cdmo.1 (reset: Nov 1, 10:57 PM per the model menu; Flash, 3.1 Pro and Argon limited). Resume at queue index 55 (ind-cdmo.1).
  • Pass 9b QUOTA at contact-locations.1 (reset: Nov 2, 3:57 AM per the model menu; Flash, 3.1 Pro and Argon limited). Resume at queue index 79 (contact-locations.1); 2 items left.

To carry on when the quota resets: the image-prompt-loop skill, stage 3, with research/pass9b/GEN-BRIEF.md; the queue is research/pass9b/queue.json (sections still waiting are marked on Concepts). Then describe the new images (stage 1) so the atlas covers them.

The art directions we rotated

From the prompt kit (kit.json). Neighbouring sections never share one.

  • isometric technical line drawing of white polypropylene equipment, catalogue illustration, uniform hairline strokes, isolated on the ground, no shading, no hatching
  • technical blueprint on deep navy, pale blue-white hairline line art, one continuous double-line pipe in steel blue linking every item, P&ID valve symbols at the joints
  • engineering drawing sheet on navy, zone-reference border and title block, mono document codes, hairline table rules
  • limestone paper drawing sheet with a fine navy border, title block bottom right, navy hairline diagram, numbered notes in a narrow column
  • instrument-panel readout: one oversized light numeral with its unit, a fine tick scale and a single limit line with a small outlined limit tag
  • editorial magazine spread, dramatic asymmetric layout, oversized light-weight headline cropped by the frame, one striking line-drawn figure, hairline rules
  • Swiss International Typographic Style, strict modular grid of square navy and limestone tiles, huge light numerals with slash, one tile holds a blueprint drawing
  • long page alternating navy drawing bands and limestone reading sheets, each band one picture
  • one matte white polypropylene skid in soft 3D isometric render, even studio light, translucent pale-blue water, hairline leader lines to labels
  • macro close-up of a polypropylene butt-fusion weld or membrane, duotone navy and limestone, shallow depth of field, crisp hairline annotations over it

The prompt for the new take
Generate an image. Design ONE section of a website as a single flat desktop UI mockup image: a 1440 px wide web page section, straight-on, no device frame, no browser chrome, no people, no photographs. Company: Aquemi, a small Canadian engineering firm that designs and fabricates modular polypropylene Purified Water systems (pretreatment, reverse osmosis, EDI, storage and distribution loop) for pharmaceutical and medical-device plants. Readers are process engineers, validation leads and quality heads who read specifications closely. Visual language: deep navy (#0F2A47), warm limestone off-white (#EFE7DD), paper white, a single steel-blue accent (#2F6FA3) used only for lines and one highlight; ultra-fine 1.5 px technical line drawings like engineering blueprints, P&ID schematics and isometric equipment; light-weight Geist sans headlines, monospace for figures and standard codes; square corners, hairline rules, drawing-sheet details (title blocks, dimension lines, grid ticks, zone letters, revision marks) quietly filling the negative space. The section is on the page 'Home' and is titled 'One package, one water path'. It must communicate:  - Pretreatment : Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pretreatment protects the reverse osmosis (RO) membranes from chlorine, chloramine and particles.;  - PW generation : RO and deionization on a PP skid, designed to meet the USP conductivity and organic carbon limits.;  - Storage and distribution : PP tank and loop: turbulent flow at peak demand, sanitized by [PP loop sanitization method].;  - Monitoring and controls : Online total organic carbon (TOC) and conductivity, with audit trails.. Make it a moonshot: the most striking, inventive, award-level layout for exactly this content that you can imagine, bold and stylish yet calm and precise, visual first: let drawings, flowing water paths, annotated equipment, instruments, gauges, stamps or diagrams carry the meaning, and keep text to short labels. Avoid plain rows, generic card grids and ordinary tables; if a table is truly right, make it an extraordinary one. Surprise me.

Make it a moonshot: the most striking, inventive, award-level layout for exactly this content that you can imagine, bold and stylish yet calm and precise, visual first: let drawings, flowing water paths, annotated equipment, instruments, gauges, stamps or diagrams carry the meaning, and keep text to short labels. Each Gemini original was read back into text: what style family it belongs to, its palette, type, composition and layout devices, the motion it implies, 25 to 40 text-to-image keywords, a content-free prompt that would make it again, what works, what fails, and how well it fits the brand (1 to 5). Click an image for its full description. The 34 pass 9b images are not described yet (image-prompt-loop, stage 1).

The conclusions: the brand core, the ten families, what combines well, what fails and how to say so in a prompt, the prompt kit, and three ways to unify the looks. Numbers in boxes open that image. Source: design-system/inspiration/style-atlas/STYLE-ATLAS.md.

Style atlas: what 94 Gemini images say about the Aquemi look

This atlas covers every Gemini image made for the site (../gemini/01–). It is for designers and for anyone writing image prompts. It records what keeps showing up, what works, what fails, and the vocabulary to prompt with. It does not replace the brand book (../../README.md); where the two disagree, the brand book rules until someone changes it.

brand_fit (1–5) in every description scores an image against the brand book as it is written today (calm, light type, line art, one accent). It does not score boldness or quality. The owner wants bolder, award-level sections, so a low score on a strong idea (, ) means "needs reworking to fit", not "reject".

1. Corpus and method

Images94 (– early concepts and drawings: 30; – later passes: 37; – pass 9, varied art directions: 27)
Section kindsequipment drawing 21, spec/limits 11, process diagram 8, router 8, standards 8, options 7, steps/timeline 6, documents 5, hero 3, whole page 3, other 3, FAQ 2, closing 2, case study 2, icon/spot sheet 2, form 1, footer 1, nav 1
Brand fitmean 3.67. Scores: 5 ×10, 4 ×51, 3 ×25, 2 ×8. By era: early 3.43, later 3.97, pass 9 3.52
Top rated (5), , , , , , , , ,
Lowest (2), , , , (off-offer subjects: WFI, steam, stainless), , , (heavy type or photo props)

Method. Each image was described once by an image-to-text pass into images/<same stem>.json. The schema has these fields: style_family, art_direction, composition, layout_devices, palette, typography, rendering, line_and_texture, motifs, ui_patterns, motion_implied, mood, t2i_keywords, t2i_prompt, signature_idea, strengths, weaknesses and brand_fit. aggregate.py (standard library only) turns those descriptions into keywords.json:

  • phrases_by_field: every phrase in every field, normalised (lowercase, spelling merged, plurals folded), with the number of images it appears in.
  • concepts: about 90 curated regex concepts that merge different wordings of one idea ("deep navy background", "navy page ground" → navy_ground). Each concept has image counts, its share in each era, mean fit with and without it, and its files. A phrase starting with "no …" counts as a negation, never as the thing it negates.
  • families: one primary family per image, assigned by ordered rules plus 4 overrides (, , , ; the reasons are in the script).
  • cooccurrence, brand_fit (by era, family and section, and the fit lift of each concept), era_shift, t2i_vocabulary, negations.

All counts below are images, not mentions. They come from keywords.json.

Re-run after adding or re-describing images. Write one JSON per new gemini/NN-*.png in images/, using the same schema, then run:

python design-system/inspiration/style-atlas/aggregate.py

Then update the counts here. A new image's family comes from FAMILY_RULES, so check the printed family table and add an OVERRIDES entry if a hybrid lands in the wrong family.

8. Prompt kit

Assemble prompts as base + one style module + one section module + content + negatives. Keep the content to the section's real words, or use <CONTENT> with placeholders. Never copy figures back out of an image.

Base block (the brand core in t2i vocabulary):

A 1440 px wide desktop website section, flat straight-on UI mockup, no device frame, no people. Aquemi, maker of modular polypropylene Purified Water systems for pharmaceutical plants. Palette: deep navy (#0F2A47) and warm limestone off-white grounds, pure white, one steel-blue accent used as a line or a single figure. Large light-weight sans-serif headline in sentence case, monospace only for figures, units and standard codes. Square corners, hairline 1–1.5 px rules and line drawings, numbered items, generous negative space. Calm, precise, engineered. Show one idea clearly with at most five labelled items.

Style modules (pick one, 1–2 lines each):

FamilyModule
1 Equipment line artisometric technical line drawing of white polypropylene equipment, catalogue illustration, uniform hairline strokes, isolated on the ground, no shading, no hatching
2 Navy pipe-routetechnical blueprint on deep navy, pale blue-white hairline line art, one continuous double-line pipe in steel blue linking every item, P&ID valve symbols at the joints
3 Navy sheet UIengineering drawing sheet on navy, zone-reference border and title block, mono document codes, hairline table rules
4 Limestone sheetlimestone paper drawing sheet with a fine navy border, title block bottom right, navy hairline diagram, numbered notes in a narrow column
5 Instrumentinstrument-panel readout: one oversized light numeral with its unit, a fine tick scale and a single limit line with a small outlined limit tag
6 Editorialeditorial magazine spread, dramatic asymmetric layout, oversized light-weight headline cropped by the frame, one striking line-drawn figure, hairline rules
7 Swiss / bentoSwiss International Typographic Style, strict modular grid of square navy and limestone tiles, huge light numerals with slash, one tile holds a blueprint drawing
8 Page rhythmlong page alternating navy drawing bands and limestone reading sheets, each band one picture
9 Soft 3D (rare)one matte white polypropylene skid in soft 3D isometric render, even studio light, translucent pale-blue water, hairline leader lines to labels
10 Macro (rare)macro close-up of a polypropylene butt-fusion weld or membrane, duotone navy and limestone, shallow depth of field, crisp hairline annotations over it

Section modules:

SectionModule
Heroheadline and one lead line left, the page's equipment drawing right with leader-line callouts to three key figures
Spec / limitslimits as rows: parameter, mono value with unit, standard reference. One row highlighted in steel blue
Process / stepsstages strung along one continuous pipe, numbered 01–05, each with a short title and what it leaves behind
Routerthree to five situations on the left, each routed by one line to its system and first step
Standards / evidenceeach standard code in mono, joined by a hairline to the part of the plant it governs and to its proof document
Documentsdocuments as a register or binder index: code, title, revision, who signs
Optionsoptions shown on the skid they attach to, each a numbered module on the drawing
Band / closingone large light statement, one measured figure as proof, one action

Example prompts

  1. Limits as a Swiss readout grid (hybrid 2): [base] + "Swiss International Typographic Style, strict modular grid of square navy and limestone tiles; each tile is an instrument readout with one huge light numeral, its unit in mono, a fine tick scale and a single steel-blue limit line; one tile holds a white isometric line drawing of a polypropylene skid on navy. Section: Purified Water release limits: conductivity, TOC, microbial action level, each with its pharmacopoeia reference in mono." + negatives.
  2. Standards as a sticky drawing (hybrid 3): [base] + "Left 60 %: a pinned navy blueprint cutaway of white polypropylene pipework and a storage tank in hairline line art, the active part outlined in steel blue. Right: limestone drawing sheets stacked on a thin vertical rail, each with a title block, a mono standard code, what it requires and the document that proves it." + negatives.
  3. Scope as a battery-limit split (hybrid 4): [base] + "Section split exactly in half, navy left, limestone right; the vertical seam is the battery limit. Left: what Aquemi supplies, as numbered hairline-framed items. Right: what the site provides. Tie-in points (feed water, drain, power, compressed air) are small P&ID nodes sitting on the seam, each labelled in mono. Light headline crossing the seam." + negatives.

9. Toward unification

Three ways to unify the families into one system:

A. Drawing setB. Measured editorialC. Material and line
IdeaThe site is a set of engineering drawings. Every section is a different sheet type: general arrangement (GA), P&ID, schedule, detail, datasheet, register. Variety comes from sheet type, not art direction. This is the current site, made consistent.Editorial-scale light typography and numbers do the shouting: huge light headlines, figures as heroes, Swiss tiles and splits. Line drawings appear as figure plates with leaders. Variety comes from scale, crop and grid.The line-drawing system above, plus a rare "material moment" per page: a matte PP render, a duotone macro of a weld or membrane. It shows the product's real material, which no line drawing can.
Core keywordsblueprint, navy ground, limestone sheet, title block, zone frame, P&ID, one continuous pipe, hairline, mono codesoversized light headline, giant light numerals, Swiss grid, asymmetric spread, split seam, hairline rules, figure plate, leader calloutswhite polypropylene, matte render, translucent water, duotone macro, hotspots, sticky reveal, plus the A keywords
Absorbs1, 2, 3, 4, 8 (68 images)5, 6, 7, with 1 and 4 as figure plates9, 10, with 1 and 2 as the base
System impactTokens unchanged. Components: a shared sheet frame / title-block primitive, P&ID glyph set, pipe-route primitive. Motion: line-draw and flow only.Tokens: add a display-xxl step (light 300, clamp to about 160 px), a display size for mono numerals, tile grid spacing, a navy/limestone tile pair. Components: ReadoutGrid, Split (seam), EditorialSpread, FigurePlate. Motion: count-up, mask-reveal type, light kinetic type.Tokens: an image treatment (duotone navy/limestone map), a render ground. Components: StickyStory (pin + rail), Hotspot. Assets: a real Aquemi 3D model and macro photos. Motion: ScrollTrigger pin/scrub.
RiskBlueprint everywhere, which the owner already rejected. Dense: 14 of 16 navy-route images flaggedBold type drifts back to heavy caps (19 images failed on that). Needs strict "light only" rulesGlossy and stock look (, , ), wrong-material renders (, ), needs assets that do not exist yet

Recommendation: B as the spine, A as its drawing language, C as a capped accent. That means:

  • Measured editorial sets the page's voice. Big light type, numbers as heroes, Swiss/split grids for variety and "chaos".
  • Drawings and data always appear together (line art + table: 17 images, mean fit 4.24, the best pairing in the set). The drawing set supplies every figure, so blueprint becomes one sheet among many instead of the whole page.
  • At most one material moment (render or duotone macro) per page, only of real PP equipment.
  • Per page: one loud section (hybrid 1, 4 or 5), the rest calm. Never two adjacent sections in the same family.
  • Two changes to the brand book make this possible: allow light display type well above display-xl, and loosen Motion for one pinned or scrubbed story per page.

This keeps what the ten five-rated images share: all ten have a navy ground, a steel-blue accent, hairline strokes and mono figures, and eight of the ten have a light headline, line art and square corners. It also delivers the boldness the owner asked for through scale and composition, not through the heavy type, glow and props that cause the low scores.

What each builder did, page by page: the look per section, the concept idea kept, the art direction borrowed, what was cut, and what was still weak.

Motion

  • ApprovalMerge: 15 counts up, lanes run down, rows rise, nodes land, wires run into the bus, the stamp strikes. ~3 s.
  • RetrofitPlant: AQiso draws the plant and runs the water at full strength, then the plant drops to existing and the picked upgrade lights; tabs and panel rise. < 5 s. Tab click/arrow keys relight the sheet (CSS fade).
  • StrikeGaps: per row: gap set, strike darkens through it, arrow runs, fix rises. ~1.3 s/row.
  • ReviewReticles: per frame: brackets close in, drawing prints up, scan line sweeps once, text rises. ~1.5 s/row.
  • CutoverSchedule: water line runs to the shutdown, the gap opens with its label, line runs on; bars grow in step, hold diamond and stamp strike. ~3.5 s.
  • motioncheck 1280 and 375: 0 errors, 0 hidden.

Skill · .claude/skills/image-prompt-loop/

Image to text to image for Aquemi design work. Describe generated or reference images as text-to-image keywords and prompts, aggregate them into the style atlas (families, brand core, anti-patterns, prompt kit), then write new section prompts from the kit and generate concepts in Gemini through Claude in Chrome by editing the chat's first prompt. Use when someone asks to analyse the images we have made, find our visual style or keywords, refresh the style atlas, write image prompts for site sections, generate new Gemini concepts, or "run the image loop".

Tools: describe.workflow.js, gemini-helpers.js, kit.json, save_capture.py, section_prompts.py

Image prompt loop: image → text → image

Three stages that can run alone or as a loop. Everything lives in this repo:

WhatWhere
Every Gemini original, numbered oldest firstdesign-system/inspiration/gemini/NN-<kind>-<subject>.png (+ README tables saying what each was prompted for)
One JSON description per image (image → text)design-system/inspiration/style-atlas/images/<image>.json
Aggregation (re-runnable, stdlib) and its outputdesign-system/inspiration/style-atlas/aggregate.py → keywords.json
The atlas: brand core, families, intersections, anti-patterns, prompt kit, unification optionsdesign-system/inspiration/style-atlas/STYLE-ATLAS.md
Prompt kit as data (base, art-direction modules, negatives)tools/kit.json (next to this file)
Section prompts from page filestools/section_prompts.py
Gemini helpers (edit-first-prompt, capture)tools/gemini-helpers.js
Describe workflow (fan-out image → text, then synthesis)tools/describe.workflow.js

1. Image → text (describe)

For new images (or the whole set), run the describe workflow with the file names as args (an array): Workflow({scriptPath: ".claude/skills/image-prompt-loop/tools/describe.workflow.js", args: ["95-....png", ...]}). It needs the user's opt-in to a workflow; without one, do the same by hand or with one subagent per ~11 images: Read each image and write style-atlas/images/<name>.json in the schema in the script (SCHEMA_TEXT: style_family, art_direction, composition, layout_devices, palette, typography, rendering, line_and_texture, motifs, ui_patterns, motion_implied, mood, 25–40 t2i_keywords, a content-neutral t2i_prompt, signature_idea, strengths, weaknesses, brand_fit 1–5). Describe what is in the image, not what it should be. The synthesis agent then re-runs aggregate.py over ALL JSONs and rewrites STYLE-ATLAS.md. Already-described images keep their JSON; only pass new ones.

2. Text: read the atlas before prompting

STYLE-ATLAS.md §2 (brand core), §3 (families and their risks), §5 (intersections and hybrids to try next), §7 (anti-patterns and the negative keywords), §8 (prompt kit), §9 (unification options and the recommendation). When the atlas changes, update tools/kit.json (pre = base block, directions = style modules, suf = quality bar + negatives) so new prompts follow it.

3. Text → image (generate in Gemini)

  1. Prompts: python tools/section_prompts.py tools/kit.json <queue.json> [page ids] writes one item per section (key, dir, mid). Art directions rotate in shuffled rounds so neighbours differ. Hand-edit a mid when a section deserves a specific idea (e.g. a hybrid from atlas §5).
  2. Gemini (gemini.google.com, model Pro, through Claude in Chrome; one tab, the only tab in the group, no new chats):
    • Send the first prompt by typing it (any section), so the chat has one user message.
    • Set window.PRE/window.SUF from kit.json, then paste tools/gemini-helpers.js into one javascript_exec. It stores the helpers in localStorage.p9.
    • Per image, one browser_batch: load helpers if missing (eval(trustedTypes.createPolicy('p'+Date.now(),{createScript:s=>s}).createScript(localStorage.p9)) — plain eval is blocked), await go(<mid>), computer wait 10 s ×4 + 8 s, navigate to the chat URL (a reload: after a generation, screenshots of the tab often freeze), wait for model-response img, load helpers, await cap(), computer zoom region [0,0,w*0.6125,h*0.6125] with save_to_disk:true, scale:1, ovx(). Then python tools/save_capture.py <key> <saved png> <h> <out dir> (crops to the real height; keeps earlier takes as .vN). Gemini returns 1024 px wide images of varying height (572–718).
    • Editing the first prompt each time gives a fresh, context-free generation (earlier images do not steer it). To regenerate the same prompt, change a word (" Take 2."): identical text leaves Update disabled.
    • Do not download images from the page (the second automatic download raises Chrome's multiple-downloads prompt and freezes the tab); do not fetch blobs (CSP); never long JS waits (they freeze the tab).
    • Quota: the reply "I can create more images as soon as your limit resets" ends the run; the model menu shows the reset time per model (all models share it). Stop and build with what exists.
    • Judge each image as it lands: keep it when one clear visual idea explains the content; regenerate once when it is generic (text over wallpaper, stacked boxes, plain table) or fell back to blueprint against its direction.
  3. Keep every image: copy to design-system/inspiration/gemini/NN-<kind>-<subject>.png (next numbers), add rows to the README table (what it was prompted for, the idea), run python tools/gallery.py, then describe them (stage 1) so the atlas stays complete.
  4. Make it readable: python tools/research.py rewrites research.html (the Design research page on the site: every concept beside the section it became, every description, the themes, atlas, build notes and this skill) and copies the pass's text records from ../research/pass9* into the repo's research/. Run it after each of stages 1 and 3.

Loop

generate (3) → describe (1) → re-aggregate → read what scored and what failed (2) → adjust kit.json and the mids → generate. Each turn of the loop should move one thing: a family to retire, a hybrid to try, a negative to add.

Rules

  • Images are ideas, never facts: never copy figures, standards, claims or logos out of an image into the site.
  • Aquemi offers polypropylene Purified Water packages only: prompts and judgements reject stainless, WFI, pure steam, stills and orbital welding (atlas §7: 30 images went off-offer).
  • Screenshots and image views cost tokens: view each generated image once, at capture; use the JSON descriptions for everything after.

The prompt kit

Prompt kit for section concepts, from design-system/inspiration/style-atlas/STYLE-ATLAS.md section 8. pre + mid + suf is what Gemini receives; mid comes from section_prompts.py. Edit directions to steer variety; keep the base and negatives in step with the atlas.

Base (before the section)

Generate an image. A 1440 px wide desktop website section, flat straight-on UI mockup, no device frame, no people. Aquemi, maker of modular polypropylene Purified Water systems for pharmaceutical plants. Palette: deep navy (#0F2A47) and warm limestone off-white grounds, pure white, one steel-blue accent used as a line or a single figure. Large light-weight sans-serif headline in sentence case, monospace only for figures, units and standard codes. Square corners, hairline 1–1.5 px rules and line drawings, numbered items, generous negative space. Calm, precise, engineered. Show one idea clearly with at most five labelled items.

Section part

The section's heading and real content, written by section_prompts.py from the page file, then one art direction.

Ending (after the section)

 This should look like award-winning web design (Awwwards Site of the Day): genuinely original, one memorable central idea that explains the content, strong typographic hierarchy, bold use of scale and space. Keep text to short labels. Show the whole section. Avoid: no bold or heavy headline, no condensed display type, no italic display, no all-caps headline, no monospace body text, no rounded corners, no pills, no glow, no bloom, no neon, no lens flare, no gradients except a faint ground, no drop shadows, no glossy reflections, no photographs, no stock props, no clipboards, no toolboxes, no laptops, no people, no lab coats, no water splashes, no droplets, no molecules, no globes, no stainless steel, no tri-clamps, no orbital welding, no distillation columns, no steam generators, no red, no green, no orange, no beige, no kraft paper, no device frame, no micro text, no duplicated labels, no slogans, no decorative connector lines.

Art directions

  • isometric technical line drawing of white polypropylene equipment, catalogue illustration, uniform hairline strokes, isolated on the ground, no shading, no hatching
  • technical blueprint on deep navy, pale blue-white hairline line art, one continuous double-line pipe in steel blue linking every item, P&ID valve symbols at the joints
  • engineering drawing sheet on navy, zone-reference border and title block, mono document codes, hairline table rules
  • limestone paper drawing sheet with a fine navy border, title block bottom right, navy hairline diagram, numbered notes in a narrow column
  • instrument-panel readout: one oversized light numeral with its unit, a fine tick scale and a single limit line with a small outlined limit tag
  • editorial magazine spread, dramatic asymmetric layout, oversized light-weight headline cropped by the frame, one striking line-drawn figure, hairline rules
  • Swiss International Typographic Style, strict modular grid of square navy and limestone tiles, huge light numerals with slash, one tile holds a blueprint drawing
  • long page alternating navy drawing bands and limestone reading sheets, each band one picture
  • one matte white polypropylene skid in soft 3D isometric render, even studio light, translucent pale-blue water, hairline leader lines to labels
  • macro close-up of a polypropylene butt-fusion weld or membrane, duotone navy and limestone, shallow depth of field, crisp hairline annotations over it

Section types skipped: faq, related, form, contact-routes.

Skill · .claude/skills/motion-library/

Find, port and ship motion for the Aquemi site from the Subframe Motion library (309 MIT React/WebGL examples - shaders, scroll stories, counters, buttons, diagrams) into our vanilla JS + GSAP stack and design tokens. Use when someone asks for an animation, a hover or press effect, a scroll reveal, a shader or ambient background, "more motion", "use Subframe", or to make a section feel alive; also before writing any new motion.js from scratch.

Tools: motion.py

Motion library: Subframe Motion → Aquemi

Subframe Motion (https://www.subframe.com/motion) is a library of 309 open-source (MIT) motion examples in three categories: Components & interactions, Animation & motion, WebGL & shaders. The examples are React (some need the motion package) or raw WebGL. Our site is vanilla JS, GSAP 3.13 and design tokens, so we port examples: keep their motion mechanism and values, rewrite the shell.

WhatWhere
MCP server (Claude Code loads it from the repo's .mcp.json)subframe-motion → https://mcp.subframe.com/motion/mcp, no account. Tools: search_motion_examples, get_motion_example, get_motion_guidance
Same calls without the MCP (subagents, scripts)`python .claude/skills/motion-library/tools/motion.py search "<words>" \get <slug> --out <dir> \guide <topics> \catalog`
Every example: slug, category, runtime, look, descriptioncatalog.json (next to this file; refresh with motion.py catalog)
What we ported, where it livesthe table below (keep it current)
Our WebGL runtime (ambient layers)assets/src/motion/gl.js (AQgl.def, AQgl.scan) + component FxShader
Our GSAP layerassets/src/motion/core.js (AQmotion.fx, helpers m.on, m.tw, m.claim, m.split, m.count…)

Finding the right example

  1. Say what the section must explain, then what should move (atlas and brand book first: steady flow, hairline, navy/limestone, one steel-blue accent). Search in plain words, several phrasings; filter --runtime webgl or --category. Browse catalog.json by look when the words don't hit.
  2. get <slug> --out <scratch dir>: read motion, adapt (names the code that drives the motion), reducedMotion, limitations, packages, assets, license. Read guide adapting once, and scroll / ambient / text-and-numbers / feedback for that kind of effect.
  3. Reject examples that need photos or assets we don't have, or that would read as consumer/playful (stickers, physics toys, emoji, audio). Never stainless/chrome/brushed-metal looks: Aquemi is polypropylene only.

Porting rules

  • Keep: the mechanism (the shader, the spring or easing values, the stagger, the geometry), its reduced-motion branch and keyboard behaviour, and the MIT licence header (paste it at the top of the ported block with Ported from Subframe Motion "<title>" (<slug>), MIT, (c) 2026 Subframe).
  • Replace: React state with DOM + GSAP (gsap.to, quickTo for pointer-follow, ScrollTrigger for scroll-linked, Flip for layout moves, SplitText for type); motion springs with GSAP eases of the same feel (aq-settle, power3.out, elastic never); demo colours with tokens (CSS var(--flow) in DOM, colors:{u_x:'flow'} in shaders); demo copy with the section's real copy.
  • WebGL: one fragment shader per effect, registered with AQgl.def('<name>', {frag, colors, uniforms, still, pointer, scale}) in the component's motion.js (runs before AQmotion.fx). Markup: host gets aq-fx-host, first child <canvas class="aq-fx-shader" data-gl="<name>" aria-hidden="true">. Multi-pass simulations (feedback buffers) need an AQgl extension; prefer single-pass analytic shaders.
  • Where the code goes: a section's effect in that look's design-system/components/<Look>/motion.js (+ style.css); a site-wide effect in the shared component (Button, RelatedLinks, FAQ…) or core.js. Never add React, the motion package or another library.
  • Tokens only in CSS; the design-system check must report 0 problems.

Motion rules (brand book, Motion)

  • Scroll-triggered reveals play once and settle within 5 s; travel ≤ 16 px for text.
  • Visitor-driven feedback (hover, press, drag, scrub) may repeat; 100–200 ms for hover/press, exits a third faster.
  • Ambient layers (FxShader): only while on screen, only the most visible one moves, one visible cycle ≥ 6 s, faint behind text, a still frame under reduced motion, at most two per page.
  • One pinned or scroll-linked story per page: readable at every scroll position, skippable, never hijacks scroll speed, static layout under reduced motion.
  • Nothing runs under prefers-reduced-motion except still frames and essential state changes.
  • Verify with research/tools/motioncheck.js <page> 1280 and 375 (0 errors, nothing left hidden) and watch the loud one with film.js.

Skill · .claude/skills/aquemi-design-system/

Change, extend, review or publish the Aquemi design system in this repo. Use when adding or editing a component, changing tokens (colours, type, spacing), adding a page-section type to the site, reviewing the visual guide, or publishing design-system changes to the Claude design system artifact.

Aquemi design system

design-system/ is the source of truth. The site (index.html), the visual guide (design-system.html) and the Claude design system artifact all come from it. Read AGENTS.md for the file map.

Change or extend

  1. Read design-system/README.md (brand book) and the README of every component you touch.
  2. Make the change:
    • Tokens: edit design-system/tokens.json. Keep the list shape {"tokens":[{"name","value","usage"}]}; colours as {"light": "#…", "dark": "#…"} hex; every token has a usage note. Text colours need 4.5:1 on their ground in both themes.
    • New component: python tools/design_system.py new <PascalName> "<Group>", then fill in README.md, preview.html (real Aquemi copy, line 1 the @dsCard marker) and style.css (tokens only).
    • Existing component: edit its style.css, README and preview together (bundle.css is generated).
    • New section type on the site: component first, then a renderer assets/src/blocks/<type>.js, then content in a page file in content/pages/, then the mapping table in design-system/page-inventory.md.
  3. Run python tools/design_system.py build and python tools/design_system.py check. Fix every problem it reports.
  4. Review visually: serve the repo (python -m http.server 8000) and open /design-system.html and the affected site pages. Check light, dark and the "Phone width" toggle on the component.
  5. Commit to main and push. GitHub Pages updates in a minute or two.

Publish to the Claude design system

The artifact is listed in design-system/artifact.json (artifact). It is a Design System artifact; its content lives in its own files under project/.

  1. python tools/design_system.py build && python tools/design_system.py check
  2. python tools/design_system.py stage <scratch dir> to copy every publishable file to <scratch dir>/project/ (it leaves out generated tokens.css, components.json and artifact.json).
  3. Read the live index with the Artifact tool: read the artifact with path: "project/design-system.json". Save a copy at <scratch dir>/project/design-system.json, keep every key as read, and only set lastChange to {"by": "<person you work for>", "at": "<now, ISO 8601>", "via": "Claude Code", "note": "<one line on what changed>"}. Change assetGroups only when assets changed.
  4. Publish in one call: url = the artifact, root = <scratch dir>, file_path = the absolute path of <scratch dir>/project/design-system.json, files = every other staged file by its project/… path (the same path on both sides). Leave out files that did not change if you prefer; files left out are kept.
  5. If the publish is refused because someone saved meanwhile, read the index again, redo step 3 once, and publish again. If refused a second time, tell the person.
  6. New logos or images: upload them first (publish with asset: true to the artifact), add the record to the index's assetGroups and the id to design-system/artifact.json, and put the file in brand/ so the guide can show it.

Never publish index.html, SKILL.md or anything under artifact-type/ to the artifact; only project/… paths.

Sharing

The artifact is shared from its page's Share menu on claude.ai. Agents can't change sharing. If a teammate can't open it, ask the owner to share it with the organization.

Pass 9 · Build brief: every section a moonshot

The owner's words, condensed: the copy is settled (plus or minus), but the site reads like dense documentation — tabular data all the way down, every section the same shape. Take each section to the next level of design: bold, unique, visual first, GSAP motion with real UI/UX excellence ("water flowing through our devices", blueprints, things appearing as you scroll). The goal is the most impressive website an industrial buyer of water systems has ever seen — and also the clearest and easiest to browse, tuned to their needs. Text may be trimmed or recast to serve the design (keep only the parts that matter, swap some lines for drawings), but never a new claim.

Each section now has a Gemini concept image: research/pass9/concepts/<page>.<blockIndex>.png (.vN = another take; research/pass9/concepts/log.md says which take is the one to build — the newest take made with an art direction wins and what idea to keep). Follow the concept's idea closely — its layout, its central visual, its composition, its density of negative-space detail — and build it to completion. Past passes lost features in the rebuild; don't. Ignore the concept's invented text, numbers, logos and standards; use the page's real content.

How a section gets its new design (no shared files touched)

  1. A look: set "look": "<name>" on the block in content/pages/NN-<page>.json. wBlock (assets/src/page.js) renders it with LOOKS['<name>'](block, headingHtml) instead of the type renderer. Without the look the block renders as before, so the old renderer stays as fallback.
  2. Renderer: assets/src/blocks/look-<name>.js registering LOOKS['<name>']=function(b,H){ return sec(H+…) } (helpers in assets/src/core.js: sec, split, tx (escapes and turns [placeholders] into the Placeholder chip — always pass copy through tx), e, wlink, tcell, wIcon, wSpot, idx, wFold/fli, wSecHead output arrives as H). Read the block's existing fields; you may add new optional fields to the block in your page file (e.g. a short label per item, x/y positions) — document them in your component README.
  3. Component: python tools/design_system.py new <PascalName> "Page sections" → design-system/components/<Name>/ with style.css (tokens only, phone rules under @container (max-width: 860px)), README.md (first sentence = summary; markup; fields; Motion paragraph), preview.html (line 1 @dsCard marker; real Aquemi copy), and motion.js (AQmotion.fx('<Name>', function(root, m){…}), see design-system/components/Hero/motion.js, LimitGauges/motion.js; API in assets/src/motion/core.js).
  4. Style varies by section on purpose (owner, 2026-11-01): concepts follow different art directions (editorial, data-viz, HMI screen, Swiss type, tactile objects, kinetic type, bento, 3D render, blueprint now and then…). Build each in ITS direction; do not convert everything back into blueprint line art. Keep brand tokens and type. Drawings: where a section needs equipment line art, use the shared isometric kit IsoKit (assets/src/parts/IsoKit.js, README in design-system/components/IsoKit/) for equipment, pipes, flow and drawing-sheet furniture, so all sections draw in one hand. If the kit lacks a part, draw it inline in your own renderer in the same style (1.5 px line-strong strokes, flow for water, round joins) and say so in your report. Line icons: wIcon(name) / wSpot(name). The page's big equipment drawing (assets/illustrations/<page>.webp, Illustration component) can also be reused.
  5. Reuse: if another builder's look fits one of your sections, reuse it (look name) rather than making a near-copy; check assets/src/blocks/look-*.js first. A look must be data-driven (no copy hard-coded in JS).

Design rules (brand, still binding)

  • Tokens only: colours (navy, limestone, surface*, ink*, line*, flow, flow-tint, status colours only in data), type classes (aq-h1, aq-lead, aq-eyebrow, aq-data/mono for figures), spacing, radius. No literal colours or px spacing in CSS. Geist / Geist Mono only. Square corners.
  • Navy blueprint grounds and limestone sheets are welcome (the concepts use them); keep text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 in both light and dark themes. Gradients: only the two allowed grounds (brand book).
  • Real text in the DOM (never baked into images/SVG <text> for content that matters — SVG <text> is fine for short drawing labels if also present as real text or aria-hidden duplicates), decorations aria-hidden, keyboard-reachable controls (≥ 44 px targets), visible focus.
  • Phone (375 px) is a first-class design, not a squeezed desktop: same character, re-composed (vertical pipe run, stacked callouts), no horizontal page scroll, text ≥ 12 px.
  • Keep every link, intent, anchor, nav, fold, form hand-off and placeholder the block has. Placeholders stay placeholders ([...]), rendered by tx.
  • Copy: you may shorten or drop lines so the design breathes (log each cut in your report with the exact text); never add a fact, number, standard, client or promise. Brand voice: sentence case, units with a space, no hype words.

Motion rules (GSAP 3.13; ScrollTrigger, MotionPath, DrawSVG, SplitText, ScrambleText, Flip, CustomEase loaded)

  • Motion explains: pipes draw on, water travels the route (a flow dash or a droplet on a MotionPath) and each stage lights as it arrives; callouts extend from the part; gauges sweep; stamps strike; layers explode apart and settle.
  • One timeline per component, triggered once on scroll-in (m.on(el, fn)); register tweens with m.tw; m.claim(el) on the root you choreograph (leave .aq-sec-head to the core). Anything moving longer than 5 s must stop.
  • Hover/press micro-interactions on interactive parts (e.g. hovering a branch highlights its route).
  • Transforms, opacity, clip-path, stroke only. Never leave content hidden at the end (motioncheck: 0 hidden). Nothing under reduced motion; the page is complete with JS off.

Checks (loop until it is genuinely excellent)

Server: http://localhost:8766 (already running from aquemi-web/; never 8765; do not start another). If your launch prompt names a port (e.g. 8768), prefix every research tool command with AQ_BASE=http://localhost:<port>/ so builders spread across servers.

  • python tools/design_system.py build then check (0 problems) and check --budgets <page>.
  • Look at your work sparingly — screenshots cost tokens: node ../research/tools/peek.js <page> 1280 <out.png> <scrollY> 900 for one viewport, and the same at 375 (height 812). Find a section's scrollY with node ../research/tools/shot.js <page> --w 1280 --out <dir> (prints the table; open only the PNG you need). Compare against the concept side by side in your head; iterate until the build carries the concept's idea and finish. Downscale before viewing when you can (python PIL thumbnail((900,900))).
  • Motion: node ../research/tools/film.js <page> 1280 <outPrefix> <scrollY> "300,900,1800,3200" (real-motion frames); node ../research/tools/motioncheck.js <page> 1280 and 375: 0 errors, 0 hidden.
  • Never run more than two browser tools at once (the local server drops connections under load).

Ownership

You own: your page file(s), the looks/components you create (their folders and look-*.js), and research/pass9/build/<page>.md (your notes). Shared files (core.js, page.js, base.css, motion/core.js, IsoKit, other builders' looks) — do not edit; append a one-line request to research/pass9/shared-requests.md. Never touch board/, export.txt, vendor-profile.md. No git (the orchestrator commits).

Report (≤ 15 lines)

Per section: look name, what the concept's idea became, motion, copy cut (exact), phone treatment; anything weak still; shared requests.

Sections without a concept of their own (Gemini quota ran out; owner: "use what we have")

Pick, from the whole concept pool (research/pass9/concepts/*.png, log in log.md; also in the gallery as design-system/inspiration/gemini/68…94-p9-*), the idea that fits that section's content best, or reuse a look another builder already made (assets/src/blocks/look-*.js) when the content has the same shape. Within one page, vary the art directions so no two neighbouring sections share one, and keep blueprint line art to at most one or two sections per page. Name the concept you adapted in your report.

Style atlas (read before designing; added mid-pass)

aquemi-web/design-system/inspiration/style-atlas/STYLE-ATLAS.md analyses all 94 Gemini images. Recommended direction: measured editorial as the spine (big LIGHT type and figures as heroes, Swiss tiles and split grids for variety), line drawings as figure plates paired with real data (line art + table is the best-scoring pairing), one material moment per page at most. Its §7 anti-patterns apply to builds too: no heavy or all-caps display type, no glow, no decorative connector lines that mean nothing, no density for its own sake, no rounded pills except standard tags.

Pass 9b · Motion: port the Subframe Motion library into the site

The owner wants the site's motion built from Subframe's "massive library of amazing motion" (https://www.subframe.com/motion: 309 MIT examples, React + WebGL). Pass 9 gave every section its own look and a GSAP timeline; this pass makes the motion world-class by porting the best-fitting library examples into our stack. The goal stays: the most impressive industrial site a water-system buyer has seen, still clear and easy to browse.

Read first

  • aquemi-web/.claude/skills/motion-library/SKILL.md — the tooling (motion.py search/get/guide, catalog.json), porting rules, motion rules. Follow it exactly. Read motion.py guide adapting plus the topics for your effects.
  • aquemi-web/design-system/README.md → Motion (rules updated for this pass: ambient layers, one pinned story per page, visitor-driven feedback may repeat).
  • aquemi-web/assets/src/motion/core.js (the GSAP layer and its helpers) and assets/src/motion/gl.js (AQgl).
  • research/pass9/BUILD-BRIEF.md — binding rules from pass 9: tokens only, real text, phone first-class, never a new claim, [placeholders] stay, links/intents/anchors kept.

How to work

  1. For each section you own: look at it once (node research/tools/shot.js <page> --w 1280 --full --out <dir>, view a downscaled copy; crop where needed — screenshots cost tokens, plan them), read its look's renderer and motion.js, then decide what the library can add: a better entrance choreography, a visitor-driven interaction (hover, scrub, drag, toggle), a scroll-linked story, or an ambient layer. Not every section needs a port; every page should gain at least two clearly better moments and one wow moment. Variety across the page: neighbours move differently.
  2. Search the library (several phrasings, browse catalog.json), get the example source into your scratch dir, port its mechanism to vanilla JS + GSAP (+ AQgl for shaders) with tokens and the section's real content. Keep the MIT header line Ported from Subframe Motion "<title>" (<slug>), MIT, (c) 2026 Subframe at the top of the ported code.
  3. Make it robust: works at 375 and 1280, in light and dark, with keyboard (interactive parts focusable, visible focus), under reduced motion (still, complete, nothing hidden), and with JS off (the static markup is complete).
  4. Verify: python aquemi-web/tools/design_system.py build, check (0 problems), and AQ_BASE=http://localhost:<your port>/ node research/tools/motioncheck.js <page> 1280 and 375 (0 errors, nothing left hidden). Watch the loud moment with research/tools/film.js (frames at intervals) and make sure every timeline ends cleanly. Serve with python research/pass9/serve.py <your port> from aquemi-web/ (run it in the background; stop it at the end). Never use port 8765; 8766 belongs to the owner.
  5. Add a row per port to the "Ported so far" table in aquemi-web/.claude/skills/motion-library/SKILL.md (append only, one line each; other agents append too — re-read before editing and edit only your rows).

Ownership

Only the files your assignment names. Shared files you don't own: append requests to research/pass9b/requests.md (one line: file, page, what, why). No git, no git stash. Never touch board/, export.txt, vendor-profile.md.

Per page or component: which examples you ported (slug → where), what is now interactive, what you rejected and why, anything still weak, requests filed.
